name: Section 8 Housing Choice Voucher (DOH statewide)
description: A HUD-funded voucher that pays part of the rent on a private apartment. DOH runs the statewide program; local housing authorities run their own lists.
eligibility: Low-income households; US citizens or eligible non-citizens. Income limits set by HUD by area.
ongoing_cost: About 30% of monthly adjusted income toward rent and utilities
max_benefit: Payment standard minus 30% of adjusted income (or gross rent minus 30%, whichever is less)
how_to_apply: Waiting list closed. Register at cthcvp.org/notifications to be told when any CT Section 8 list opens. DOH, 505 Hudson St, Hartford, CT 06106.
notes: DOH says all its HCV waitlists are closed (page dated Aug 20, 2026). About 8,911 DOH vouchers were leased in June 2025. Apply to every local housing authority list that opens.

name: Mainstream Housing Opportunities vouchers (DOH)
description: Section 8 vouchers set aside for people with disabilities. DOH fills them from its regular HCV waiting list.
eligibility: People with disabilities on the DOH Section 8 waiting list who meet HCV rules.
how_to_apply: No separate application; get on the DOH HCV waiting list when it opens (cthcvp.org/notifications).
notes: 407 Mainstream vouchers were leased in June 2025 (DOH Rental Assistance Programs report SFY25). DOH does not list NED vouchers as a separate program. The HCV list is closed.

name: CT811 Section 811 Project-Based Rental Assistance
administrator: CT Department of Housing (DOH) with CHFA, DSS, DDS, DMHAS and OPM
description: HUD-funded rent help tied to specific apartments in affordable buildings, for extremely low-income adults with disabilities. DOH refers people when a unit opens.
eligibility: Adults with disabilities aged 18 to 62 with household income at or below 30% of area median income.
ongoing_cost: Not published on DOH page (HUD 811 PRA rules normally set rent at about 30% of adjusted income)
how_to_apply: Tenants are referred by DOH. Program contact: Tawny Pho, DOH, tawny.pho@ct.gov, (860) 270-8091.
notes: FY13 grant produced 71 units; FY19 grant expects 113 units and FY23 grant (awarded Aug 2024) expects 158 units, per the DOH CT811 snapshot. Ask DDS or your case manager about a referral.

name: Fair housing and reasonable accommodation (HUD FHEO)
administrator: US Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), Office of Fair Housing and Equal Opportunity
description: Disability is protected under the Fair Housing Act and Section 504. You can ask a landlord for a reasonable accommodation or modification and report discrimination to HUD.
eligibility: Anyone who faces housing discrimination, including people with disabilities.
how_to_apply: Online at hud.gov/reporthousingdiscrimination, call 1-800-669-9777, or mail HUD form 903.1.
notes: HUD says there are time limits on filing; report as soon as possible. The state agency (CHRO) has a 300-day deadline.

name: SSI living-arrangement rules
description: Your SSI check can drop if someone else pays part of your housing costs. Paying your full share of household expenses avoids the cut.
eligibility: SSI recipients.
max_benefit: Federal SSI is $994/month in 2026; the one-third cut is up to $331.33 and the in-kind cut is capped at $351.33
how_to_apply: Call SSA at 1-800-772-1213 or visit ssa.gov/ssi.
notes: In a Medicaid institution for a full month, SSI is limited to $30 (plus any state payment). Plan rent agreements in shared or family homes with this in mind.

name: Rental Assistance Program (RAP)
administrator: CT Department of Housing (DOH), through J. D'Amelia & Associates and local housing agencies
description: A state-funded rent subsidy, similar to Section 8, for low-income renters in private housing.
eligibility: Household income generally at or below 50% of area median income; US citizens or eligible non-citizens.
ongoing_cost: 30% of income for elderly or disabled households (40% for other families)
how_to_apply: Waiting list closed. Register at cthcvp.org to be told when it reopens.
notes: About 6,433 RAP certificates were leased in June 2025. DDS buys some RAP certificates for its supportive housing model.

name: DDS Community Living Arrangements (group homes)
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS) and private providers
description: Licensed group homes, usually for up to six people, with staff support. Most are funded through the Medicaid Comprehensive Supports waiver.
eligibility: DDS-eligible adults (intellectual disability or Prader-Willi) who are given residential funding based on need.
ongoing_cost: Not published. DDS waiver funding excludes recurring room and board (DDS self-direction cost guidelines), so it comes from the person's own income.
how_to_apply: Apply for DDS eligibility, then ask your DDS case manager. DDS Help Line 860-418-6000 or 866-737-0330, ddsct.co@ct.gov.
notes: As of Dec 2025, 1,552 people were on the DDS residential waiting list (567 with no services, 310 underserved, 675 with future needs).

name: DDS Community Companion Homes (CCH)
description: A licensed family shares its home with up to three people who are eligible for DDS services. It is not a group home.
eligibility: DDS-eligible adults with residential funding.
ongoing_cost: Not published (the host family gets a DDS-set room and board rate plus a monthly stipend)
how_to_apply: Ask your DDS case manager. DDS Help Line 860-418-6000.
notes: Many private providers (Marrakech, Benhaven, Abilis, SARAH Tuxis) run CCH or shared living programs.

name: DDS Continuous Residential Supports and Individualized Home Supports
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS) and private providers
description: CRS supports up to three people sharing a house or apartment with staff available 24 hours. IHS brings a tailored package of support to a home the person chooses.
eligibility: DDS-eligible adults with residential funding.
ongoing_cost: Rent and food are paid by the person; DDS funding covers support staff
how_to_apply: Ask your DDS case manager. DDS Help Line 860-418-6000.
notes: IHS is a common route for adults who want their own apartment.

name: DDS Supportive Housing (non-project-based)
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS), using DOH RAP certificates
description: DDS pairs a rental subsidy with support from an IHS provider so a person can live in an ordinary apartment.
eligibility: DDS-supported adults with intellectual disability and low income (under 50% of area median income). Providers identify candidates.
ongoing_cost: No more than 30% of adjusted income (SSI counts)
max_benefit: Rent above 30% of income, within the subsidy limit
how_to_apply: Ask your DDS case manager or IHS provider.
notes: The posted notice was rolling until funds ran out and ran through Dec 2024. Whether there is a 2026 round is not published.

name: DDS Community-Based Housing Subsidy
description: A DDS subsidy that covers part of the housing costs for people receiving DDS residential services whose income cannot cover them.
eligibility: People receiving DDS residential services. Assets must be under DSS state-supplement limits and income under HUD very-low-income limits. Other funding must be tried first.
ongoing_cost: About 45% of adjusted monthly income (a 20% wage disregard applies)
max_benefit: The person keeps $400 to $600 a month after rent
how_to_apply: Ask your DDS case manager. DDS, 460 Capitol Ave, Hartford, CT 06106.
notes: The procedure was last revised in 2009. Funding for new applicants depends on each year's budget.

name: DDS Comprehensive Supports Waiver
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS) with DSS (Medicaid)
description: A Medicaid waiver that funds licensed residential settings, in-home supports, day and job programs, and specialized supports.
eligibility: DDS-eligible, Medicaid-eligible, needs ICF/IID level of care. The budget is based on the DDS Level of Need assessment.
ongoing_cost: None for services (room and board not covered)
max_benefit: Individual budget set by Level of Need (no published cap)
how_to_apply: Through your DDS case manager. DDS Help Line 860-418-6000.
notes: The self-direction cost guidelines (June 2025) allow up to $35,000 per waiver period for home modifications and $2,000 per move for apartment setup.

name: DDS Individual and Family Support Waiver
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS) with DSS (Medicaid)
description: A Medicaid waiver for in-home supports, respite, day and job services, and some residential options (fewer than the Comprehensive waiver).
eligibility: DDS-eligible, Medicaid-eligible, needs ICF/IID level of care. The budget is based on Level of Need.
max_benefit: Individual budget (cap not published on the DDS fact sheet)
how_to_apply: Through your DDS case manager. DDS Help Line 860-418-6000.
notes: Often used to fund supports in a family home or your own apartment.

name: DDS eligibility (intellectual disability and autism)
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS) Eligibility Unit
description: DDS adult services, including residential supports, require DDS eligibility. Autistic adults without intellectual disability are sent to the DSS Autism Spectrum Disorder program.
eligibility: Intellectual disability (full-scale IQ 69 or lower plus adaptive limits starting before age 18) or Prader-Willi syndrome. Autism without ID is handled by DSS.
how_to_apply: Send the DDS eligibility application to DDS.Eligibility@ct.gov, fax 860-622-2797, or 460 Capitol Ave, Hartford, CT 06106. Questions: 1-866-433-8192 or 860-418-6117.
notes: Testing should be done before age 18; a standardized autism test must be done before age 21.

name: DSS Autism Waiver (Home and Community Supports Waiver for Persons with Autism)
description: A Medicaid waiver for autistic people without intellectual disability. It pays for life-skills coaching, job coaching, community mentoring, respite and live-in companions, but not rent or placements.
eligibility: Autism diagnosis, no intellectual disability (IQ 70 or higher), substantial limits in 2+ life areas starting before age 22, Medicaid-eligible, age 3+.
max_benefit: Up to $50,000 per person per year in services
how_to_apply: DSS Autism waiver: Susan Stange, 1-800-445-5394 option 6, Susan.Stange@ct.gov. ASD program: 860-424-5677, Nathaniel.Calixto@ct.gov.
notes: Not an entitlement. 2,652 people were on the waitlist in April 2026 and some have waited more than 10 years (CT Public). This is the main state route for autistic adults without ID.

name: DSS State Supplement to the Aged, Blind or Disabled
description: A needs-based state cash supplement for people on SSI or Social Security disability. DSS budgets your rent and living costs against your income and pays the gap.
eligibility: Ages 18-64 with a permanent disability (or 65+ or blind); income under 3 times the SSI maximum; assets $1,600 single or $2,400 married.
max_benefit: Varies; the shelter allowance in the budget is capped at $400 living alone or $200 living with others
how_to_apply: Apply at connect.ct.gov or call 1-855-626-6632 (TTY 1-800-842-4524).
notes: The 2026 Medicaid state plan amendment (CT-26-0004) disregards the 2.8% Social Security COLA so it does not reduce the supplement. The supplement also brings Medicaid coverage.

name: CHFA Disabled Persons Homeownership Program (Home of Your Own)
description: A below-market first mortgage with an extra 0.125% rate discount for buyers with a disability in the household.
eligibility: A documented disability for a household member (SSI, DSS or DDS proof); first-time buyer (or no home in 3 years); within CHFA income and price limits.
upfront_cost: Down payment and closing costs (down payment help available)
how_to_apply: CHFA (860) 721-9501, customer.service@chfa.org, 1-844-CT1-HOME.
notes: Can pair with CHFA Time to Own down payment help (up to $25,000 forgivable, per DOH).

name: Loans and Grants for Accessibility (AccesSolutions)
administrator: Corporation for Independent Living (CIL), funded by CT DOH
description: Grants for home accessibility changes such as ramps and accessible bathrooms, secured by a lien on the home.
eligibility: Household income at or below 100% of area median income.
ongoing_cost: None (a lien is placed on the home)
how_to_apply: Apply on cil.org (AccesSolutions form) or call (860) 563-6011; 57 Charter Oak Ave, Suite A, Hartford, CT 06106.
notes: CIL says funding is extremely limited right now. DOH lists this program as active (page dated Aug 12, 2026).

name: Connecticut Home Improvement Program (CHIP)
administrator: Capital for Change with CT DOH
description: A low-interest loan to repair or improve a 1-4 unit home you own and live in.
eligibility: Low- or moderate-income owner-occupants of 1-4 unit homes.
how_to_apply: Kristen Fusco, Capital for Change, 860-761-1627, KFusco@capitalforchange.org.
notes: Useful for families adapting a home where an autistic adult will live.

name: Money Follows the Person (MFP)
description: Helps people move out of a nursing home or other long-term care facility into the community with Medicaid supports.
eligibility: People living in a nursing home or other long-term care facility; full rules are in the DSS FAQ.
how_to_apply: Apply online at dss-hcbs.service.ct.gov/communityoptions.
notes: Only for people currently in an institution. DOH also has a Section 8 preference for MFP and nursing facility transitions.

name: CHRO Housing Discrimination Unit
administrator: CT Commission on Human Rights and Opportunities (CHRO)
description: The state civil-rights agency takes housing discrimination complaints, including disability-based ones.
eligibility: Anyone who faces housing discrimination in Connecticut.
how_to_apply: Call 860-541-3403 or 800-477-5737 ext. 3403 (TDD 860-541-3459), or use the online inquiry form at portal.ct.gov/chro.
notes: File within 300 days.

name: 2-1-1 Connecticut and Coordinated Access (housing crisis)
administrator: United Way of Connecticut (2-1-1) with CT DOH Coordinated Access Networks
description: Dial 2-1-1 for housing crisis help. A specialist screens you and connects you to shelter diversion and your regional Coordinated Access Network.
eligibility: Anyone in Connecticut facing homelessness or a housing crisis.
how_to_apply: Dial 2-1-1, option 3 (Mon-Fri 8:30-4). TTY 1-800-671-0737. Online at 211ct.org.
notes: This is the front door for homeless services statewide.

name: CTHousingSearch.org
description: A free statewide search for rental listings, including accessible units, with email alerts.
eligibility: Anyone.
how_to_apply: Search at cthousingsearch.org or call 1-877-428-8844 (Mon-Fri 9am-8pm).
notes: Useful once you have a voucher or RAP certificate.

name: My Place CT
description: The state's No Wrong Door website for long-term services, with housing planning pages for older adults and people with disabilities.
eligibility: Anyone.
how_to_apply: Visit myplacect.org; call 2-1-1 for help.
notes: Run with CMS support.

name: Housing Authority of the City of Hartford
administrator: Housing Authority of the City of Hartford (HACH)
description: Runs federal public housing, Section 8 vouchers and RAD properties in Hartford.
eligibility: Low-income households within HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Call 860-723-8400; 180 John D. Wardlaw Way, Hartford, CT 06106; hartfordhousing.org.
notes: Public housing list closed Sep 4, 2026, then a Sep 9, 2026 notice announced a reopening. Check the site for current status. HCV list status not stated.

name: Elm City Communities (New Haven Housing Authority)
description: New Haven's housing authority. It runs public housing, Section 8 vouchers and Elderly and Disabled resident services.
eligibility: Low-income households within HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Call 203-498-8800 (TDD 711); 360 Orange St, New Haven, CT 06511; elmcitycommunities.org.
notes: Section 8 waitlist closed effective May 1, 2026.

name: Park City Communities (Bridgeport Housing Authority)
description: Bridgeport's housing authority. It runs Section 8 vouchers, family housing and buildings for seniors and people with disabilities.
eligibility: Low-income households within HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Call 203-337-8900; 150 Highland Ave, Bridgeport, CT 06604; apply online at parkcitycommunities.org.
notes: Waitlist status not stated on the site.

name: Charter Oak Communities (Stamford Housing Authority)
description: Stamford's housing authority. It runs Section 8 vouchers and 21 owned properties.
eligibility: Low-income households within HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Call 203-977-1400 (TTY 1-800-842-9710); 22 Clinton Ave, Stamford, CT 06901; charteroakcommunities.org.
notes: A 'Waitlists Opening' notice was posted Sep 30, 2026; check which lists are open.

name: Norwalk Housing
description: Norwalk's housing authority, with about 1,067 Section 8 vouchers, 1,084 public housing units and a homeownership voucher.
eligibility: Low-income households within HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Call 203-838-8471 (TDD 800-545-1833 x437); 24 1/2 Monroe St, Norwalk, CT 06854; norwalkha.org.
notes: Waitlist status not stated on the site.

name: Waterbury Housing Authority
description: Runs Section 8 vouchers and public housing in Waterbury.
eligibility: Low-income households within HUD income limits.
how_to_apply: Call 203-596-2640; info@waterburyha.org; 2 Lakewood Rd, Waterbury, CT 06704.
notes: Waitlist status not stated on the site.

name: Chapel Haven Schleifer Center
description: Residential education and supported-living programs (REACH, SLP, SAIL) for adults with autism and intellectual disabilities on a New Haven campus.
eligibility: Adults with autism or intellectual/developmental disabilities.
ongoing_cost: Not published (private pay, with scholarships available)
how_to_apply: Call 203-397-1714; 1040 Whalley Ave, New Haven, CT 06515; chapelhaven.org.
notes: Active in 2026 (2026 auction, page updated Oct 2026). Has an autism transition program (ASAT).

name: Benhaven
description: Group homes and shared living (Community Companion Homes) for people with autism and developmental disabilities.
eligibility: People with autism or developmental disabilities, usually DDS-funded.
how_to_apply: Call (203) 239-6425; 187 Half Mile Rd, North Haven, CT 06473; benhaven.org.
notes: Active in 2026 (events Jul-Aug 2026).

name: Oak Hill
description: Connecticut's largest private disability services provider. It runs group homes and individual homes for people with intellectual, developmental and physical disabilities.
eligibility: People with disabilities, usually DDS-funded.
how_to_apply: Call (860) 242-2274 (TTY 860-286-3113); 120 Holcomb St, Hartford, CT 06112; oakhillct.org.
notes: Active in 2026 (Summer 2026 newsletter).

name: Ability Beyond
description: Residential living and Community Companion Home programs for adults with disabilities in Connecticut and New York.
eligibility: Adults with disabilities, usually DDS-funded.
how_to_apply: Call (888) 832-8247; info@abilitybeyond.org; 4 Berkshire Blvd, Bethel, CT 06801.
notes: Site updated May 2026.

name: Marrakech
description: DDS group homes, Community Companion Homes, shared living and Continuous Residential Supports.
eligibility: People with disabilities, usually DDS-funded.
how_to_apply: Call (203) 389-2970; 6 Lunar Dr, Woodbridge, CT 06525; marrakechinc.org.
notes: Active in 2026 (Jul-Sep 2026 newsletter).

name: Journey Found
description: Residential, independent-living and family-home supports for adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
eligibility: Adults with IDD, usually DDS-funded.
how_to_apply: Call (860) 643-9844; info@journeyfound.org; 60 Hilliard St, Manchester, CT 06042.
notes: Active in 2026 (event Oct 29, 2026).

name: SARAH Tuxis Residential and Community Resources
description: Shoreline provider of CLAs, Continuous Residential Supports, Individualized Home Supports, Community Companion Homes and shared living.
eligibility: DDS-funded adults in Branford, Clinton, East Haven, Guilford, Madison, Milford, New Haven, North Branford, Old Saybrook, Stratford, West Haven and Westbrook.
how_to_apply: Call (203) 458-8532; 45 Boston St, Guilford, CT 06437.
notes: DDS provider profile updated 5/27/2025. Its sister agency SARAH Inc. (sarah-inc.org) runs day and job services, not housing.

name: Abilis
description: Lower Fairfield County provider of CLAs, CRS, Community Companion Homes, live-in caregiver and shared living.
eligibility: DDS-funded adults in Darien, Greenwich, New Canaan, Norwalk, Ridgefield, Stamford, Weston, Westport and Wilton.
how_to_apply: Call (203) 531-1880; 50 Glenville St, Greenwich, CT 06831.
notes: DDS provider profile updated 6/9/2026.

name: CLASP Homes
description: 11 group homes and 9 supported apartments with 24-hour support for adults with autism and developmental disabilities in Fairfield County.
eligibility: Adults with autism or developmental disabilities.
how_to_apply: Call (203) 226-7895; 246 Post Road East, Westport, CT 06880; clasphomes.org.
notes: Site shows Sep 2026 images.

name: Corporation for Independent Living (CIL)
description: A nonprofit developer that builds community residences for people with disabilities and runs the state-funded AccesSolutions accessibility program.
eligibility: Providers, families and low-income homeowners needing accessibility work.
how_to_apply: Call (860) 563-6011; 57 Charter Oak Ave, Suite A, Hartford, CT; cil.org.
notes: Active in 2026 (CIL Golf 2026).

name: ASRC at Clifford Beers (Autism Services & Resources Connecticut)
description: Autism information, a resource line and a statewide resource directory. It is not a housing provider but helps families find adult services.
eligibility: Autistic people and families.
how_to_apply: Main (203) 772-1270; Resource Line 203-265-7717 (Mon-Thu 9:30-3); directory.ct-asrc.org.
notes: ASRC joined Clifford Beers in 2023. Page updated Mar 2026.

name: The Arc Connecticut
description: Statewide advocacy group for people with IDD and their families, with a network of local Arc chapters, many of which run residential programs.
eligibility: People with IDD and families.
how_to_apply: thearcct@gmail.com; 141 Weston St, PO Box 142, Hartford, CT 06141; thearcct.org.
notes: Active in 2026 (Harvest of Hope 2026). Its housing guide 'The Journey to Community Housing with Supports' is posted by DDS.

name: Connecticut Fair Housing Center
description: A nonprofit that helps with housing discrimination complaints and has a disability letter generator for accommodation requests.
eligibility: Anyone facing housing discrimination in CT.
how_to_apply: Call 860-247-4400 or 888-247-4401; info@ctfairhousing.org; 60 Popieluszko Ct, Hartford, CT 06106.
notes: Active in 2026 (posts through Aug 2026).

name: Ticket to Work
description: Free, voluntary program that lets SSDI/SSI beneficiaries get job training, placement and ongoing support from Employment Networks or state VR (BRS) while protected from medical continuing disability reviews.
eligibility: Ages 18-64 receiving SSDI and/or SSI because of a disability.
how_to_apply: Call the Ticket to Work Help Line 1-866-968-7842 (TTY 1-866-833-2967), Mon-Fri 8am-8pm ET, or choose an Employment Network (CT ENs include Ability Beyond and The Kennedy Collective).
notes: Verified Oct 2026.

name: Plan to Achieve Self-Support (PASS)
description: Lets a person set aside income or resources toward a specific work goal (training, equipment, job coaching, business startup) without it reducing SSI.
eligibility: SSI recipients (or SSDI recipients who could become SSI-eligible) with a feasible work goal.
max_benefit: Set-aside amounts are not counted for SSI; no fixed dollar cap published
how_to_apply: Complete Form SSA-545-BK and submit to local Social Security office; BRS counselors, WIPA/benefits counselors and Employment Networks can help write it.

name: SSI/SSDI work incentives (SGA, Trial Work Period, Student Earned Income Exclusion)
description: Rules that let disability beneficiaries test work and keep some or all benefits: 2026 SGA $1,690/mo (blind $2,830), Trial Work Period month counts at $1,210/mo, and SSI students under 22 can exclude up to $2,410/mo ($9,730/yr).
eligibility: SSDI beneficiaries (SGA, TWP); SSI recipients (earned income exclusions; SEIE for students under 22 regularly attending school).
how_to_apply: Report earnings to SSA; get a free benefits analysis from a BRS Benefits Specialist (CWIC) before changing work hours.
notes: SSI earned income: first $20 general + $65 then half of the rest excluded (ssa.gov/ssi/text-income-ussi.htm).

name: Section 1619(b) Medicaid While Working (Connecticut threshold)
administrator: Social Security Administration with CT Dept. of Social Services (Medicaid)
description: SSI recipients whose earnings end their SSI cash payment can keep Medicaid (HUSKY) as long as earnings stay under a state threshold; Connecticut's 2026 threshold is $55,480 per year.
eligibility: Was eligible for SSI for at least one month, still disabled, needs Medicaid to keep working, and earnings below the CT threshold (individualized threshold possible if higher medical costs).
max_benefit: Medicaid continues up to $55,480/yr gross earnings in CT (2026)
how_to_apply: Automatic through SSA when earnings stop SSI cash; confirm with local SSA office or a BRS Benefits Specialist.
notes: CT is not listed in the blind-beneficiary table.

name: Work Opportunity Tax Credit (WOTC)
administrator: IRS / U.S. DOL; certified in CT by CT Department of Labor WOTC Unit
description: Federal employer tax credit for hiring people in targeted groups (including VR referrals and SSI recipients). Authority LAPSED for anyone starting work on or after January 1, 2026; no reauthorization as of the latest check.
eligibility: Employers hiring targeted-group workers; only hires who started on or before 12/31/2025 can currently be certified.
max_benefit: Was $2,400-$9,600 per hire; currently no credit for 2026 hires unless Congress reauthorizes retroactively
how_to_apply: CTDOL still accepts Form 8850 (via CTHires or mail to 200 Folly Brook Blvd, Wethersfield, CT 06109, Attn: WOTC Unit; DOL.WOTC@ct.gov) and holds 2026-start requests pending reauthorization.
notes: Lapse confirmed by CRS report R43729 (May 13, 2026). Show as 'lapsed' in UI.

name: AbilityOne Program (CT nonprofit agencies)
administrator: U.S. AbilityOne Commission with SourceAmerica and NIB
description: Federal contracting program where nonprofit agencies employ people who are blind or have significant disabilities to make products and provide services (custodial, food service, admin) for the federal government.
eligibility: People who are blind or have significant disabilities; participating nonprofits must perform at least 75% of direct labor hours with such workers.
how_to_apply: Find affiliated Connecticut agencies via the AbilityOne PLIMS reports (plims.abilityone.gov/reports) or contact SourceAmerica/NIB.
notes: Specific CT AbilityOne agencies not verified individually.

name: Job Accommodation Network (JAN)
administrator: U.S. DOL Office of Disability Employment Policy
description: Free, confidential expert advice on workplace accommodations and ADA employment rights for workers, job seekers and employers.
eligibility: Anyone (job seekers, employees, employers, families).
how_to_apply: Call (800) 526-7234 or use AskJAN.org live chat.

name: Schedule A hiring authority (federal jobs)
description: Lets federal agencies hire qualified people with intellectual, severe physical or psychiatric disabilities without competing through the regular process.
eligibility: Person with intellectual, severe physical or psychiatric disability who is qualified for the job; needs a Schedule A proof-of-disability letter (doctor, licensed VR specialist such as BRS, or benefits agency).
how_to_apply: Note Schedule A eligibility on USAJOBS applications, or send resume + Schedule A letter to an agency's Selective Placement Program Coordinator.
notes: Eligibility does not guarantee a job; probation up to 2 years possible.

name: BRS Vocational Rehabilitation (VR)
administrator: CT Bureau of Rehabilitation Services (BRS), Dept. of Aging and Disability Services (ADS)
description: Individualized help to prepare for, find and keep a job (assessment, training, job coaching, accommodations, benefits counseling) under an Individualized Plan for Employment. BRS is operating under an Order of Selection: only Priority Group 1 (most significant disabilities) is being served; Groups 2 and 3 are closed with a waiting list.
eligibility: Physical or mental disability (including autism) that makes it hard to get or keep a job and need for VR services; legally blind applicants go to BESB. Under 18 requires parent/guardian.
ongoing_cost: Not published (some services may consider financial need)
how_to_apply: Use the BRS online referral form or call the nearest BRS office (e.g., Hartford 860-697-3550, New Haven 203-974-3000, Bridgeport 203-683-0500, Norwich 860-848-5950, Waterbury 203-578-4550). People in closed groups should still apply to join the waiting list, served by eligibility date.
notes: OOS fact sheet is undated; status (Group 1 open, 2-3 closed) current on ct.gov as of Oct 2026. Apply guide: portal.ct.gov/ads/knowledge-base/articles/employment-services/for-job-seekers/how-to-start-your-journey-with-the-bureau-of-rehabilitation-services

name: BRS Pre-Employment Transition Services / Level Up (students)
administrator: CT Bureau of Rehabilitation Services (BRS), ADS
description: Career exploration, work experience, workplace readiness, self-advocacy and college/training counseling for students with disabilities before they leave school.
eligibility: Students with disabilities ages 16-22 (Level Up); BRS suggests starting about two years before school exit.
how_to_apply: Submit the Level Up contact form on the ADS site; a BRS counselor contacts the family.
notes: Federal Pre-ETS are funded by the VR grant; CT brands its student program 'Level Up'.

name: DDS Employment and Day Services (Employment First)
description: DDS-funded individual supported employment, customized employment, group supported employment, self-employment help, Employment Transition Services (up to 3 years) and day supports, under DDS's Employment First policy that treats community jobs as the first option.
eligibility: Adults found eligible for DDS (intellectual disability, or autism under DDS eligibility rules); hours based on Level of Need score; Medicaid waiver enrollment typically required.
max_benefit: Not published (hours set by Level of Need allocation)
how_to_apply: Apply for DDS eligibility; then contact DDS (860-418-6000, toll-free 866-737-0330, ddsct.co@ct.gov) and pick a qualified provider or self-direct.
notes: DDS and BRS signed a Competitive Integrated Employment Transformation Plan (April 2025).

name: CT Project SEARCH (17 host sites)
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS) with provider agencies and school districts
description: Nine-to-ten-month, full-immersion internship at a host business (mostly hospitals and colleges) teaching job skills, ending in job placement help.
eligibility: Transition-age students and young adults eligible for DDS services who need intensive employment skills training.
how_to_apply: Contact CT Project SEARCH Coordinator Brian Gresko (brian.gresko@ct.gov) or the provider for your area. FY2026-27 sites include UConn Health/Farmington (Favarh), Hartford Hospital & Goodwin Univ. (MARC of Manchester), Hospital of Central CT (CCARC), Backus Hospital (UCP Eastern CT), Middlesex Hospital (MARC Community Resources), Masonicare (Midstate Arc), Albertus Magnus (Ability Beyond), Charlotte Hungerford (Litchfield ARC), Greenwich & Stamford Hospitals and Darien YMCA (Abilis), Norwalk CC, Nuvance Norwalk, Danbury & Waterbury Hospitals (Ability Beyond), Woodruff YMCA Milford (The Kennedy Collective).
notes: Program page: portal.ct.gov/dds/searchable-archive/employmentdayservices/projectsearch/project-search

name: CT American Job Centers (CT Department of Labor)
description: Free career counseling, resume help, workshops, job fairs, WIOA job training and the CTHires job board, in person and virtually.
eligibility: Any job seeker.
max_benefit: WIOA training funds vary; not published
how_to_apply: Request services at ctdol.jotform.com/CT1/requestemploymentservices or visit a full-service center: Bridgeport, Hartford, Montville, New Haven, Waterbury (Hamden closed; use New Haven). Main line (860) 263-6000.
notes: Affiliate centers in 14 other towns; ask about BRS co-located staff and accommodations.

name: MED-Connect (Medicaid for Employees with Disabilities)
description: Full HUSKY/Medicaid coverage for working people with disabilities, with much higher income and asset limits than regular Medicaid; some pay a monthly premium.
eligibility: Medically certified disability or blindness and working for pay; income up to $85,000/yr (some from employment); countable assets up to $20,000 individual / $30,000 couple.
ongoing_cost: No premium below 200% FPL; above that 10% of income over the limit; max 7.5% of net family income for 250-450% FPL
how_to_apply: Apply through DSS (ct.gov/dss or ConneCT); ask a BRS Benefits Specialist for help.
notes: Medically-improved group: earnings at least 40x federal minimum wage. Premium rule for 200-250% FPL not stated on page.

name: BRS Benefits Counseling (Connect to Work Center)
administrator: CT Bureau of Rehabilitation Services (BRS), ADS
description: Benefits Specialists (Community Work Incentive Coordinators) explain how a job will affect SSI, SSDI, State Supplement, Medicare and Medicaid, and how to use work incentives like MED-Connect.
eligibility: People receiving or applying for disability cash/medical benefits who want to work.
how_to_apply: Call the Connect to Work Center 800-773-4636 or the nearest BRS office and ask for a Benefits Specialist.
notes: 'Connect-Ability' brand not found on current ct.gov pages; SSA's WIPA grantee for CT not confirmed on an official page.

name: JobsCT Tax Rebate - IDD hiring enhancement
administrator: CT Department of Economic and Community Development (DECD)
description: State rebate of 25% (50% in distressed municipalities/Opportunity Zones) of income-tax withholding for net new jobs; since 1/1/2024 (CGS 32-7t) companies hiring people with intellectual or developmental disabilities can qualify with fewer jobs and get added incentives.
eligibility: Employers creating net new full-time jobs (standard minimum 25 FTEs, $37,500+ salary); lower thresholds/extra rebate for IDD hires - must tell DECD at application.
max_benefit: 25%-50% of withholding; IDD bonus amount not published
how_to_apply: Apply through DECD JobsCT page; contact Tricia Paesani (860) 500-2415, Tricia.Paesani@ct.gov.
notes: Old CT Vocational Rehabilitation Job Creation Tax Credit ($200/mo per hire) ended for hires on/after 1/1/2012 - not listed. No other CT disability-hiring credit found.

name: DSS Waiver for Persons with Autism (job coaching)
description: Medicaid waiver for autistic people without intellectual disability that funds job coaching, life skills coaching, community mentoring and respite.
eligibility: Autism diagnosis with full-scale IQ 70+, substantial limits in 2+ major life activities, onset before 22; not an entitlement - waiting list applies.
max_benefit: $50,000 per participant per year (all waiver services combined)
how_to_apply: Contact DSS Autism Spectrum Disorder unit via ct.gov/dss (55 Farmington Ave, Hartford) to request waiver application/waitlist placement.
notes: Waitlist was 2,058 people as of 2/16/2024 (CGA presentation, Mar 2024); current figure not published.

name: Autism Spectrum Disorder Advisory Council
administrator: CT Office of Policy and Management (OPM)
description: Statewide council advising OPM and DSS on autism policy and programs, including adult services; meetings and documents are public.
eligibility: Open to public attendance.
how_to_apply: See meeting schedule and documents on the OPM council page; OPM, 450 Capitol Ave, Hartford, CT 06106.
notes: Advisory body, not a direct service.

name: Hartford Commission on Disability Issues
description: City commission that identifies needs of Hartford residents with disabilities and recommends fixes to barriers to full participation.
eligibility: Hartford residents.
how_to_apply: Call Hartford 311 at (860) 757-9311; agendas/minutes on meetinginfo.org.
notes: No employment service of its own; advocacy/referral.

name: New Haven Commission on Disabilities
description: Mayor-appointed commission working to reduce physical and attitudinal barriers facing New Haven residents with disabilities.
eligibility: New Haven residents.
how_to_apply: Contact through the City of New Haven boards & commissions page.
notes: No direct contact listed on page.

name: Bridgeport Commission for People with Disabilities
administrator: City of Bridgeport, Dept. of Health & Social Services
description: Advises the mayor on making the city accessible and inclusive; links to local disability service providers and ADA complaint form.
eligibility: Bridgeport residents.
how_to_apply: Contact Nadine Douglas, 999 Broad St, Bridgeport; 203-332-8330; meetings 2nd Thursday 6pm on Teams (none July/Aug).

name: New Haven Youth @ Work
administrator: City of New Haven Youth and Recreation Department
description: City-run paid summer (5 weeks, up to 25 hrs/wk) and year-round (up to 10 hrs/wk) jobs for New Haven youth at CT minimum wage.
eligibility: New Haven youth ages 14-21 in 9th grade or higher.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Youth @ Work page; call 203-946-7582. Ask about accommodations; BRS Level Up students can request support.
notes: Page shows 2024-25 cycle; disability supports not described - unverified for 2026 cycle.

name: Amrita Foods allergen-free bakery
description: Allergen-free snack company whose Bridgeport bakery provides jobs to young adults on the autism spectrum.
eligibility: Young adults on the autism spectrum (hiring through company).
how_to_apply: Contact the company via amritahealthfoods.com.
notes: Mission-driven employer, not exclusively autistic workforce. Covered by News 12 CT, Apr 27, 2026.

name: BeanZ & Co. inclusive cafe
description: Inclusive coffee cafe and caterer that employs people with and without intellectual and developmental disabilities.
eligibility: Adults with IDD (and others).
how_to_apply: Visit 11 East Main St, Old Avon Village (Mon-Sat 8am-4pm); 860-321-7549, beanzandco@gmail.com.
notes: Site shows 2026 menus; founding partner of AllWorkCT (Oct 2025).

name: Abilis employment services and social enterprises (Abilis Gardens & Gifts, Courthouse Cafe)
description: Greenwich nonprofit providing job training and supported employment; runs Abilis Gardens & Gifts (retail training site, 50 Glenville St, Greenwich) and cafes including the Abilis Courthouse Cafe in Stamford Superior Court staffed by adults with disabilities.
eligibility: People with disabilities in lower Fairfield County; typically DDS- or BRS-funded.
how_to_apply: Contact Abilis via abilis.us; Courthouse Cafe at 123 Hoyt St, Stamford (weekdays 7:30am-3pm).
notes: Abilis active as Project SEARCH provider in FY2026-27 DDS list; individual shop/cafe 2026 status not confirmed on official page (abilis.us blocks fetch).

name: Easterseals Capital Region & Eastern CT - Career Development Services and EnviroClean
description: Job skills, education and placement support for people with disabilities, plus social enterprises EnviroClean (eco-friendly cleaning that creates jobs for people with disabilities) and EnviroShred.
eligibility: People with disabilities (BRS community rehabilitation provider for Northern region and Windham/New London counties).
how_to_apply: 100 Deerfield Rd, Windsor, CT 06095; 860-270-0600.
notes: Also runs Veterans Rally Point.

name: The Kennedy Collective - employment services and social enterprises
administrator: The Kennedy Collective (formerly The Kennedy Center)
description: Workforce development, transition services, Ticket to Work Employment Network, work incentive counseling, and social enterprises in logistics, grounds/landscape, facilities/custodial and staffing that employ people with disabilities.
eligibility: People with disabilities; BRS/DDS-funded or Ticket holders.
how_to_apply: 2440 Reservoir Ave, Trumbull, CT 06611; 203-365-8522.
notes: Also Project SEARCH provider at Woodruff Family YMCA, Milford.

name: Goodwill of Western & Northern Connecticut - employment services
administrator: Goodwill of Western and Northern Connecticut, Inc.
description: DDS-qualified individualized and group supported employment, customized employment, prevocational and transition services in 95 towns; BRS community rehabilitation provider.
eligibility: Adults with intellectual disability (DDS) or BRS consumers.
how_to_apply: 165 Ocean Terrace, Bridgeport, CT 06605; (203) 368-6511; employment director (203) 910-3903.
notes: DDS profile updated Jan 6, 2025.

name: Goodwill of Southern New England - Employment Services (CT campus)
description: Individual employment support, engagement and recreation services for people with disabilities, plus business services for employers.
eligibility: People with disabilities and other barriers.
how_to_apply: 432 Washington Ave, North Haven, CT 06473; (203) 777-2000.

name: Ability Beyond - Employment Programs
description: Career exploration, job search/placement, interview prep, accommodation negotiation, job coaching and long-term support; Ticket to Work Employment Network.
eligibility: Ages 14+ in CT with funding from BRS, BESB, DMHAS, DDS, Ticket to Work, schools or private pay.
how_to_apply: See abilitybeyond.org/contact-us.
notes: Site active May 2026; Project SEARCH provider at Albertus Magnus, Danbury, Waterbury and Nuvance Norwalk.

name: Chapel Haven CareerAbility
description: Employment division serving adults with autism and developmental disabilities: career advising, internships (retail, food service), group and individual job coaching, customized employment and placement.
eligibility: Chapel Haven residents and community members with developmental disabilities or autism; BRS/DDS/DSS funding or scholarships.
how_to_apply: 1040 Whalley Ave, New Haven, CT 06515; 203-397-1714.
notes: Reports 90%+ reach 90 days employed (self-reported).

name: Favarh (The Arc of the Farmington Valley) - Project SEARCH at UConn Health
description: Arc chapter offering employment supports; runs the Project SEARCH internship at UConn Health, where 98% of interns over 10 years found independent jobs.
eligibility: Adults with IDD (DDS-eligible for Project SEARCH).
how_to_apply: Contact Favarh (Canton) via favarh.org or DDS Project SEARCH coordinator.
notes: Founding partner of AllWorkCT. favarh.org blocks automated fetch.

name: Marrakech - employment supports
description: DDS-qualified group supported employment, customized employment and prevocational services for adults with intellectual disability.
eligibility: Adults with intellectual disability funded by DDS.
how_to_apply: 6 Lunar Dr, Woodbridge, CT 06525; (203) 389-2970.
notes: DDS profile updated 6/10/2024.

name: Wells Fargo Center for Neurodiversity and Inclusive Employment (UConn)
description: Connects neurodivergent job seekers with neuroinclusive employers through its Neuroinclusive Candidate Network, and trains employers to build neurodiversity hiring programs.
eligibility: Neurodivergent students and job seekers; employers.
how_to_apply: Join the Neuroinclusive Candidate Network via the center's website.
notes: Founded with Wells Fargo grant (fall 2024).

name: MARC of Manchester - Project SEARCH (Hartford Hospital, Goodwin University)
description: Provider agency running Project SEARCH internships at Hartford Hospital and Goodwin University.
eligibility: DDS-eligible young adults.
how_to_apply: Contact MARC of Manchester or DDS Project SEARCH coordinator (brian.gresko@ct.gov).
notes: Only verified via DDS list.

name: ABLE CT (Connecticut ABLE savings account)
administrator: Connecticut Office of the State Treasurer (program manager: Ascensus, through the National ABLE Alliance)
description: A savings and investment account for a person with a disability. Money in it can pay for disability-related costs like housing, transportation, education and support services. Up to $100,000 does not count against the Supplemental Security Income (SSI) resource limit, and Medicaid (HUSKY) is kept no matter how big the balance is.
eligibility: Disability began before age 46, and the person either gets SSI or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) because of a disability, is blind under Social Security rules, or has a similarly severe disability with a written diagnosis signed by a physician. Eligibility must be re-certified every year. From January 1, 2026, the age limit went up from 26 to 46.
upfront_cost: You can open an account with as little as $1.
ongoing_cost: Annual account fee of $56 ($14 each quarter), or $31 a year if you choose electronic delivery. Investment costs run 0.28% to 0.34% a year, depending on the investment option.
max_benefit: Contributions up to $20,000 a year. Account owners who work can add more, up to the one-person federal poverty level or their gross wages, whichever is less. Connecticut taxpayers can deduct contributions from state income of up to $5,000 a year (single filers) or $10,000 (joint filers).
how_to_apply: Open online at ct.SaveWithABLE.com, or call (888) 609-3268.
notes: The state tax deduction figures come from the Treasurer's January 20, 2026 press release: https://portal.ct.gov/ott/newsroom/news/news-releases/senator-blumenthal-and-treasurer-russell-announce-expanded-able-ct-eligibility. If the balance goes over $100,000, SSI is suspended until the balance drops back under the limit. Proof of eligibility is not needed to open an account, but keep the diagnosis or benefit letter on file.

name: PLAN of CT Special Needs Trusts (pooled, third-party and self-settled)
administrator: PLAN of CT (Planned Lifetime Assistance Network of Connecticut), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
description: A nonprofit that runs special needs trusts. These trusts let a person with a disability have extra money and still keep public benefits like SSI and Medicaid. Parents can set up a third-party trust, often funded through their will. The pooled trust lets the person with a disability put in their own money, such as an inheritance, back payments from Social Security, or extra monthly income, and still qualify for Medicaid waiver programs.
eligibility: Connecticut residents with a disability. Third-party trusts are funded by anyone other than the person with the disability. Self-settled trusts are for people under 65 using their own money. PLAN says the pooled trust is a good idea for a person of any age with a disability whose income or assets are over the limits for home care or waiver programs.
upfront_cost: A one-time establishment fee, due when your attorney submits the trust paperwork. The amount is in a fee schedule on PLAN's site; it is not stated on the page. Attorney fees are separate.
ongoing_cost: No fees until the trust has money in it. After that, fees follow PLAN's fee schedule (amount not stated on the page).
how_to_apply: Call 860-523-4951, email info@planofct.org, or mail P.O. Box 290937, Wethersfield, CT 06129-0937.
notes: The site footer says 2023 and the linked fee schedule PDF is from 2023, so ask PLAN for current fees. PLAN says no minimum funding is required. After the person dies, money left in the pooled trust goes to PLAN's Charitable Trust or repays the state for Medicaid. Money left in a self-settled trust must first repay Medicaid.
to_check: PLAN of CT's site and fee schedule are dated 2023; ask for current fees.
apply_steps: Call PLAN of CT to talk or meet with the Outreach Coordinator about which trust fits.
Choose and meet with a PLAN of CT Professional Member attorney (the map and list are on PLAN's website).
Fill out the legal forms (Trust Adoption Agreement or Subscriber Agreement) with your attorney, plus the supporting documents.
Send PLAN of CT a check for the one-time establishment fee.

name: PLAN of CT Charitable Trust Grants
description: A one-time grant for a Connecticut resident with a disability. It pays for a specific item or service that improves their quality of life. Past grants have paid for ramps and lifts, home changes, and music therapy for a child with autism. The money goes straight to the vendor.
eligibility: Connecticut residents of any age with a disability who show financial need. People with low income and few assets get priority.
how_to_apply: Download the adult grant application from the page, or call (860) 523-4951 for a printed copy. Send the completed application by mail (PLAN of CT Outreach Coordinator, P.O. Box 290937, Wethersfield, CT 06129-0937), email (info@planofct.org) or fax ((860) 523-0267).
notes: Grants cannot replace public benefits, pay off debt, repeat, or cover basic needs like groceries or rent. Incomplete applications are not reviewed. No deadlines are posted. The site footer is dated 2023, so call to confirm the grant is still open.
to_check: PLAN of CT's site is dated 2023; call to confirm grants are still offered.
apply_steps: Download the Adult Grant Application from PLAN's Charitable Trust page, or call PLAN for a paper copy.
Gather proof of disability, your income, asset and expense details, and proof of financial need.
Get a quote or invoice for the specific item or service. Include proof of ownership if the request is for a vehicle or home change.
Mail, email or fax the complete packet to the PLAN of CT Outreach Coordinator.
The Trust Committee decides, and you get a letter by mail the week after the meeting. If approved, PLAN pays the vendor directly.

name: Connecticut Energy Assistance Program (CEAP)
administrator: CT Department of Social Services (DSS), with local Community Action Agencies (CAAs)
description: Helps pay winter heating costs. The money is usually paid straight to your utility or fuel company. You have to apply again every season.
eligibility: Connecticut residents with household income at or below 60% of State Median Income. The annual limit is $48,714 for 1 person, $63,703 for 2, $78,692 for 3, and $93,681 for 4. Households that get SNAP, Temporary Family Assistance (TFA) or SSI may qualify through those benefits. A household member with a disability who does not get benefits like SSI can file a Certification of Disability form.
max_benefit: $355 to $705 for the 2026-2027 season, depending on household size, income and heating source.
how_to_apply: Online at https://dss.service.ct.gov/ceap/s/MyDashboard. You can also call or visit your local Community Action Agency to apply by phone, email, mail or in person (for example, CRT Greater Hartford (860) 560-2694, CAANH Greater New Haven (203) 387-7700).
notes: Bring your latest electric bill and income proof. Income proof may not be needed if everyone in the household gets SNAP, TFA, SSI or another qualifying DSS benefit. The income limits come from the DSS 'Who Is Eligible' page, which does not say which season they apply to. The full list of agencies is at https://portal.ct.gov/dss/economic-security/winter-heating-assistance/energy-assistance---winter-heating/how-to-apply.

name: Low Income Discount Rate (LIDR) and Matching Payment Program – Eversource and UI electric customers
administrator: Eversource and United Illuminating (UI), under rules from the CT Public Utilities Regulatory Authority (PURA)
description: A monthly discount on the electric bill for low-income customers who have a 'financial hardship' status on their account. Hardship customers who are behind on their bills can also get their payments matched through the Matching Payment Program.
eligibility: Low-income electric customers with a financial hardship status on their utility account. For the Matching Payment Program, you also need a past-due balance of $100 that is more than 60 days old.
max_benefit: Eversource: five tiers, from 5% to 50% off. UI: two tiers, 10% or 50% off.
notes: Eversource customers can ask to be moved to a different tier if they think they belong in one. Applying for CEAP through your local Community Action Agency is a common way to get hardship status.

name: Generation Power CT (formerly Operation Fuel) – Emergency Fuel and Utility Assistance
administrator: Generation Power CT (GPCT), formerly Operation Fuel
description: A nonprofit that gives emergency grants for delivered heating fuel or past-due utility bills. There is separate help for water bills. You can get one fuel or utility grant every 12 months.
eligibility: Households earning up to 75% of State Median Income, based on household size and gross income. Utility applicants need a past-due bill in a household member's name and records of at least four monthly payments in the last 12 months. Everyone in the household age 21 and older must show income for the 4 weeks before applying.
how_to_apply: Apply online at gpct.org during an open cycle, or get in-person help at an Application Support Center. Phone (860) 243-2345, Monday–Friday 9:00am–12:00pm. Email applications@gpct.org.
notes: Applications are only accepted during three short windows. The first 2026-2027 window (Sept 1–15, 2026) has closed. All notices are sent by email, and GPCT asks people not to call to check on their application. Fuel grant details: https://gpct.org/fuel.
apply_steps: Check that your household earns no more than 75% of State Median Income (GPCT links to 211 for the income chart).
Gather income proof for everyone 21 and older (last 4 weeks), your latest past-due utility bill, and records of 4 monthly payments in the past 12 months.
Apply online at gpct.org during an open window, or get help at an Application Support Center.
Check your status by logging in to your application. Decision letters come by email.
apply_window: Dec 1–15, 2026 and Mar 1–15, 2027 (the Sept 1–15, 2026 window is closed)

name: SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) – CT DSS
description: Monthly money for groceries, loaded onto a debit-like EBT (Electronic Benefit Transfer) card. It used to be called food stamps. An autistic adult can often apply as their own household.
eligibility: Gross monthly income up to $2,660 for 1 person or $3,607 for 2 (higher for bigger households). If someone in the household has a disability or is 60 or older, the household can earn a little more than the chart and still qualify. New federal work rules (from the law known as H.R.1) affect some adults.
max_benefit: $306 a month for 1 person, $562 for 2, $808 for 3, $1,023 for 4 (figures as of October 1, 2026).
how_to_apply: Apply online at https://www.connect.ct.gov/access/jsp/access/Home.jsp, or by mail or in person. For food help, call 211.
notes: You get an answer within 30 days, or 7 days in an emergency. Most people must send in renewal forms every 6 months. DSS has prescreeners to check whether the new work rules apply to you.

name: State Supplement to the Aged, Blind or Disabled (AABD) – cash assistance
description: A monthly state cash payment that adds to other income, such as Social Security or SSI, for adults with a permanent disability. DSS compares your living costs with your income and pays toward the gap.
eligibility: Adults age 18 to 65 who meet the federal Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) disability rules and already have another source of income (Social Security, SSI or Veterans' benefits). Income must be under three times the maximum SSI amount. Assets must be no more than $1,600 for a single person or $2,400 for a married couple.
max_benefit: Not published (based on your income and needs)
how_to_apply: The program page does not list an application link or phone number. Apply through DSS; DSS's main online application is at https://www.connect.ct.gov (listed on DSS's SNAP page).
notes: Page dated February 1, 2025. It can also help pay for living in a boarding home or residential care home. Applicants must not have given away assets in order to qualify.

name: State Administered General Assistance (SAGA) – cash
description: A small monthly cash payment for adults who cannot work because of a documented medical condition. People often use it while they wait for a decision on SSI or SSDI.
eligibility: Adults who cannot work, either for now or permanently, because of a documented medical condition, or who meet other 'unemployability' rules. Income must be under three times the maximum SSI amount. Assets must be no more than $500 for a single person or $1,000 for a married couple. You cannot get SAGA if you qualify for any other state or federal cash program.
max_benefit: Not published (the page calls it a 'small cash amount each month')
how_to_apply: The SAGA page does not list an application link or phone number. Apply through DSS; DSS's main online application is at https://www.connect.ct.gov (listed on DSS's SNAP page).
notes: Page dated February 1, 2025. If an SSI application is pending, you must sign a form that lets Social Security pay DSS back for SAGA from any SSI award. One car may be excluded under certain conditions, and your home is not counted as an asset.

name: DDS Individual and Family Grants
description: Cash grants that help families pay for extra care for a family member with a disability who lives with them. Uses include in-home help, behavioral support, temporary help and crisis support (respite). Adults who live on their own and get no other DDS help at home may also qualify.
eligibility: Must be eligible for DDS services. The amount depends on the needs of the person and their caregivers.
max_benefit: The DDS grant FAQ says grants usually run $600–$1,000 a year, with up to $5,000 a year in extraordinary circumstances.
how_to_apply: Ask your DDS case manager or the DDS Regional Helpline. DDS main line: 860-418-6000; toll-free 866-737-0330.
notes: The dollar amounts come from the DDS grant FAQ that the current page links to. That FAQ sits in DDS's 'searchable archive': https://portal.ct.gov/dds/searchable-archive/family/supports-and-services/individual-and-family-grants. Confirm current amounts with your case manager. Keep receipts, because DDS may ask to see them. A not-yet-eligible autistic adult must first apply for DDS eligibility.
to_check: Grant amounts come from a DDS FAQ in its archive section; confirm current amounts with a case manager.

name: DDS Medicaid waivers – paying family members and legal guardians as caregivers
administrator: CT Department of Developmental Services (DDS), with CT DSS (Medicaid)
description: Under the DDS Medicaid waivers (Comprehensive Supports, Individual and Family Support, and Employment and Day Supports), a qualified family member or relative, including a legal guardian, can be paid to provide some supports to an adult. Examples are in-home support, individualized day supports and personal supports.
eligibility: The adult must be enrolled in a DDS Medicaid waiver. The caregiver must meet DDS qualifications and enroll with the fiscal intermediary (the payroll agency) as a Direct Support Professional, which includes a background check and training. The Employer of Record cannot also be the paid caregiver.
max_benefit: Legal guardians: a combined cap of 2,100 awake hours of support a year, and you can ask for an exception. Hourly pay rate: Not published here.
how_to_apply: Contact your DDS case manager. DDS Waiver Services email: DDS.Waiver@ct.gov.
notes: Source is the DDS HCBS Consolidated Waiver Operations Manual, Version 7, edited December 2025. Respite cannot be paid to a guardian or parent caregiver who lives with the person. Shared Living and Live-in Caregiver services cannot be provided by a legal guardian. Background: https://portal.ct.gov/dds/knowledge-base/articles/paid-family-caregivers-information (dated July 2024).

name: Community First Choice (CFC) – self-directed personal care attendants
description: A Medicaid (HUSKY) service that lets an eligible person living in the community direct their own care. That means choosing, hiring and managing their own Personal Care Attendants (PCAs) and other supports.
eligibility: Not published on the DSS page. It is for Medicaid members who need help to keep living in the community.
how_to_apply: Apply online at https://dss-hcbs.service.ct.gov/communityoptions, or dial 2-1-1 (Monday–Friday, 8:30 AM–5:00 PM) and choose Option 3.
notes: The DSS page does not say which family members can be hired as paid attendants, so ask DSS. In early 2026 the Governor proposed moving CFC participants onto waivers from April 1, 2027 (DSS FAQ dated 3.3.26). News reports in April 2026 said the proposal was dropped, but I could not confirm the final enacted budget. The DSS FAQ says self-direction would continue under waivers.
to_check: A 2026 budget proposal would move CFC participants onto waivers from April 2027; news says it was dropped, but the final budget wasn't confirmed. Also confirm which family members can be paid.

name: Connecticut Earned Income Tax Credit (CT EITC) with $250 child add-on
description: A refundable state tax credit for working people with low to moderate income. It equals 40% of the federal Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC). An adult child of any age counts as a 'qualifying child' if they are permanently and totally disabled and meet the other rules, so working parents of an autistic adult may qualify. Families with at least one qualifying child get an extra $250.
eligibility: Must qualify for the federal EITC, have earned income, and be a full-year Connecticut resident. A qualifying child can be any age if permanently and totally disabled, and must live with you in the U.S. for more than half the year.
max_benefit: Tax year 2025: up to $1,731 with 1 qualifying child, $2,861 with 2, $3,218 with 3 or more, plus the extra $250.
how_to_apply: Fill out Schedule CT-EITC with your Connecticut Resident Income Tax Return (Form CT-1040).
notes: The page shows tax year 2025 figures. A working autistic adult may also be able to claim the credit on their own return.
apply_window: Claimed on your yearly state tax return

name: Renters' Rebate for Elderly/Disabled Renters
administrator: CT Office of Policy and Management (OPM), through your town's assessor or social services office
description: A yearly cash rebate for renters with low income who are 65 or older or who have a disability. It is based on rent and utilities (not phone) paid in the previous calendar year.
eligibility: Age 18 or older and eligible to receive Social Security Disability benefits, or age 65 or older. You must have lived in Connecticut for at least 1 year, and income must be under the limits in state law (CGS Section 12-170e). Renters of an apartment, room, cooperative housing or mobile home may qualify.
max_benefit: Up to $700 for a single person, $900 for a married couple.
how_to_apply: File Form M-35r with your local town assessor's office or a social service agency. Do not send it to OPM. Questions: Renters' Rebate hotline 860.418.6377.
notes: The 2026 window (April 1–September 30) has closed. No extensions are allowed. Payments go out by November 30, and if no check arrives by December 15, call the hotline. The page mentions only Social Security Disability benefits, so people who get only SSI should ask their town whether they qualify. Expected 2027 dates are based on the page's yearly April 1–September 30 rule.

name: Totally Disabled Property Tax Exemption (home or car)
administrator: Your town Assessor's Office (program run by CT Office of Policy and Management)
description: Lowers the assessed value used for local property tax on a home or car owned by an adult who is permanently and totally disabled. There is no income limit.
eligibility: Owner is at least 18, is permanently and totally disabled, and receives Social Security disability benefits (or qualifying government retirement benefits).
max_benefit: Up to a $1,000 exemption per person
how_to_apply: Bring proof of total disability to your town Assessor's Office before the assessor files the Grand List. Forms: Taxpayer Application D-1. State contact: 860.418.6406.
notes: The $1,000 is taken off the assessed value, not off the tax bill, so the actual savings are smaller. The Grand List filing date is not stated on the page, so ask your assessor.
apply_window: Before your town's Grand List is filed (date set locally)

name: CTtransit Reduced Fare for People with Disabilities
description: Half-price bus fares for riders with a qualifying disability on CTtransit and other bus systems under contract with CTDOT. You need a CT Reduced Fare Photo ID.
eligibility: Riders with a qualifying disability under CTDOT's criteria. These include vision, hearing or mobility disabilities, or any disability that makes a person 'unable without special facilities or special planning or design to utilize mass transportation' (the federal definition). A physician's certification is needed if you don't have other proof.
upfront_cost: Not published (you pay for the physician's certification yourself)
ongoing_cost: Reduced local fares: $0.85 for a 2-hour pass, $1.70 for an all-day pass, $30.60 for a 31-day pass.
how_to_apply: Apply online at https://cttransitreducedfare.dot.ct.gov/. More info at https://www.cttransit.com/fares.
notes: Press release dated September 25, 2026. Always carry proof of eligibility when you ride. Whether a given autistic adult qualifies depends on CTDOT's review of the documents. Fare prices are from https://www.cttransit.com/fares/senior-disabled-reduced-fares.

name: Assistive Technology Loan Program (ATLP) – CT Tech Act Project
administrator: CT Tech Act Project (CTTAP), CT Department of Aging and Disability Services (ADS); loans processed by Berkshire Bank
description: A low-interest loan to buy assistive technology (AT) devices or services, like communication devices, computers or home and vehicle changes. A parent, guardian or other family member can apply for the person with a disability.
eligibility: A person with a disability (or an older adult), or their parent, guardian, family member or legal representative. The person must have lived in Connecticut for at least 1 year and have a disability that permanently affects a major life activity.
ongoing_cost: Loan payments. Interest rate: Not published.
max_benefit: Generally $500 to $30,000, repaid over 1 to 10 years.
how_to_apply: Download the application (English or Spanish) from https://cttechact.com/loan/. Phone (860) 876-9595, or toll-free in CT (800) 537-2549.
notes: Approval usually takes two weeks to a month. After approval, Berkshire Bank schedules the closing. The loan page footer says 2023, but ADS's April 14, 2026 article still lists the loan program: https://portal.ct.gov/ads/knowledge-base/articles/accessibility-services/assistive-technology/assistive-technology. CTTAP also lends devices for short trials and sells used AT at lower cost.

name: Federal Credit for Other Dependents
description: A federal tax credit for supporting a dependent who is too old for the Child Tax Credit, such as an adult child with a disability.
eligibility: Dependent of any age with an SSN or ITIN. An adult child who is permanently and totally disabled can be claimed at any age.
max_benefit: Up to $500 per dependent (nonrefundable). Phases out above $200,000 of income.
how_to_apply: Claim on Form 1040 with Schedule 8812. Free help: VITA tax sites.
notes: Nonrefundable: it lowers tax owed but is not paid out as a refund.

name: Lifeline Phone and Internet Discount
description: A monthly discount on one phone or internet plan per household.
eligibility: Anyone on SNAP, Medicaid, SSI, federal public housing and other listed programs, or with income at or below 135% of the federal poverty level.
max_benefit: Up to $9.25/month off broadband or bundled service
how_to_apply: Apply through a participating phone company or USAC's National Verifier. Lifeline Support Center (800) 234-9473.
notes: One discount per household. Eligibility is rechecked every year.

name: ACT Today! Family Grants
description: National grants for autism treatment, assessments, equipment and safety items, paid directly to approved providers or vendors.
eligibility: Families affected by autism who cannot afford a treatment or service insurance does not cover. Household income is considered.
max_benefit: Up to $5,000, paid directly to pre-approved treatment providers, assessors or materials vendors
how_to_apply: Apply online through the portal linked at act-today.org/apply-for-grant. Fall 2026 round: Sept 15 – Oct 15, 2026. Grants are awarded quarterly; check the site for the next round.
notes: National program. Does not cover transportation, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, or personal needs like rent, utilities or vacations. Decisions can take up to 12 weeks; an SOS Fund handles urgent safety needs faster.
apply_steps: Check it covers what you need: safety equipment (helmets, GPS trackers, sensory equipment, fencing), communication devices, ABA therapy, social skills programs, special-needs summer school or medical help. It does not cover transportation, hyperbaric oxygen therapy, rent, utilities or vacations.
Choose the provider or vendor. ACT Today pays them directly, not the family.
Download the Grant Application Checklist from the apply page and gather what it lists.
Apply through the online portal linked on act-today.org/apply-for-grant before the cycle closes.
Allow up to 12 weeks for a decision. If someone's physical safety is at risk, ask about the faster SOS Fund.
apply_window: Opens 4 times a year. Fall 2026 round: Sept 15 – Oct 15, 2026; check the site for the next round

name: Kodi Lee Gives Back Music Grant
administrator: Doug Flutie Jr. Foundation for Autism
description: Music scholarships for autistic teens and adults: lessons, music therapy, studio time or equipment.
eligibility: Autistic self-advocates 15 or older living in the US. Past recipients cannot reapply.
how_to_apply: Apply on flutiefoundation.org when open.
notes: 2026 round closed May 21, 2026; reopens April 2027. Foundation is based in Waltham.
apply_steps: Check eligibility: an autistic self-advocate aged 15 or older, living in the US, who hasn't received this grant before. Organizations can't apply.
Decide what to ask for: voice or instrument lessons, workshops, studio recording, music therapy, music business development, marketing or social media help, or performance opportunities.
Put April 2027 on your calendar. The 2026 round closed May 21, 2026.
Apply on the Flutie Foundation's Kodi Lee Gives Back page when it reopens. Awards are up to $1,000.

name: AANE / Flutie Foundation Grant
administrator: Association for Autism and Neurodiversity (AANE), funded by the Doug Flutie Jr. Foundation
description: Small grants for autistic adults, or parents of autistic children, for things that directly improve the person's life.
eligibility: Autism diagnosis (provider letter); living in MA or another New England state. Uses include therapies, evaluations, social skills groups, respite and uncovered health costs.
how_to_apply: Apply on aane.org and email documents (latest tax return, diagnosis letter) to grants@aane.org.
notes: Limited number of grants each year.
to_check: AANE's site blocks automated checks; application steps are from the team's Oct 5 research and were not re-checked.
apply_steps: Get a letter from a provider confirming the autism diagnosis.
Have your latest tax return ready.
Apply on aane.org, then email the documents to grants@aane.org.
Apply early in the year: AANE gives a limited number of grants. They can pay for therapies, evaluations, social skills groups, respite and health costs insurance doesn't cover.
apply_window: Not published. Limited number of grants each year
